Subject: Bulk demo: intermittent 429s during streaming export

Hi Ava / BrightLane team,

Thanks again for carving out the hour this morning for the export walkthrough. During the live run we observed repeated 429 responses midway through the streaming export for the 1.2M-row dataset — the client saw a series of short-lived 429s and the demo client retried, but it impacted the perceived throughput and caused truncated progress indicators.

Quick notes from our side:
- Issue started ~09:06 local during the first large export chunk.
- Repro rate: roughly 1 in 3 demo attempts when payloads were >10MB.
- Attached: export-logs-20261101.txt and a short screen recording.

Tessa / Marissa: I want to loop you in to decide whether we treat this as a demo-only configuration (increase demo burst) or escalate to Platform for a code-side fix.

Dev: can you take an initial look at the attached logs and confirm whether this looks like hard rate limiting at the runtime layer (429 from traffic shaping) or an upstream protective throttling? If we can turn on a demo-mode burst and increase token-bucket for the next customer meeting that would be ideal. If we need a patch to the routing/backpressure logic, please advise ETA.

Ava: can you share the precise timestamps for the next demo slot and any additional request IDs from your side (if you captured them)? That will speed up root cause mapping.

Next steps suggested:
1) Dev triage + short write-up (today)
2) Quick config change for demo (if safe) ahead of Tuesday's follow-up
3) If code change required, target a canary for Wed and a full rollout after the demo.

Thanks — Logan

2) Click export -> client opens streaming connection and receives chunks
3) After ~6-8s of steady chunks we saw first 429s; client conservatively retried twice.

We need the export to look smooth for the exec demo next Tue (2026-11-09). If you can provide any temporary config we can use to avoid this behavior for that meeting, that would be massive.

Subject: Re: Bulk demo: intermittent 429s during streaming export

Thanks for the logs and recording — I pulled runtime traces for the window you flagged. Quick triage notes:

- Observed behaviour: short-lived 429s emitted by the routing layer when token-bucket depth dropped below 0 for a given connection class. In practice this looks like aggressive backpressure kicking in for large sustained streaming throughput.
- Why it happens: our default per-tenant burst budget is tuned for steady-state multi-tenant fairness; very spiky single-tenant demo loads can exhaust the burst allotment and trigger token-bucket rejections.
- Severity: transient and self-healing (retries succeed), but bad for UX during demos.

Mitigation options:
1) Quick config (recommended for demos): temporarily increase per-tenant burst_allowance to 5x for BrightLane via runtime feature-flag. This is safe for short windows and reversible. ETA: I can flip a flag and verify within 30 minutes.

2) Near-term engineering change: relax burst accounting for streaming export endpoints by allocating a separate streaming-burst pool. Implementation requires a small change in the routing/bucket code and a canary rollout. ETA: 4 working days for PR + test + canary.

3) Long-term: adaptive burst that weights request latency and historical usage; roadmap item for Q1 2027.

Action items I need:
- Logan: confirm whether BrightLane demo window is a hard requirement before Tue 2026-11-09. If yes, I'll do (1) and document the flag and rollback steps.
- Ava / BrightLane: share any non-demo customer traffic patterns so we can tune the pool appropriately if you plan production exports at that scale.

I'll also attach the trimmed runtime trace and the minimal command to toggle the flag (see attached: export-logs-20261101.txt includes trace snippets).

Cheers,
Dev
